name: Cassava & Chrome — Oduya-Reinhardt's Last Concert, 2215
creator: Tomilola Oduya-Reinhardt (musician, sonic architect)
description: On December 31, 2215, musician Tomilola Oduya-Reinhardt performed a six-hour concert in the decommissioned Calumet Rail Yards titled 'Cassava & Chrome,' weaving live percussion traditions from West African, Eastern European, and Andean lineages through a SkinNet-shared sensory feed that allowed the 30,000 present — and an estimated 2 million remote neural listeners — to feel the resonance in their own bodies. Oduya-Reinhardt, who had been diagnosed with neural degradation from long-term SkinNet use, announced mid-performance that it would be their last. The final hour was performed in complete silence, the music transmitted only through shared BCI touch.
medium: live performance, SkinNet neural feed, physical presence
cultural_impact: Considered the definitive artistic statement on the SkinNet generation — its gifts and its costs — and cited by music scholars as the moment GLMZ produced its first globally significant artistic voice since the Collapse.
controversy: Axiom BioInterface sent a cease-and-desist over the unlicensed SkinNet mesh broadcast protocol Oduya-Reinhardt used; the letter, leaked the next day, was widely mocked as proof the company had no understanding of what it had witnessed.
story_hooks: Oduya-Reinhardt retired from public performance but never stopped composing — a locked neural archive of post-2215 work exists and its contents are unknown.

Three audience members at Cassava & Chrome experienced permanent synesthetic alterations after the silent final hour — they still perceive sound as color and have never fully explained what they heard.
A character discovers that the unlicensed broadcast protocol Oduya-Reinhardt used was not self-developed — someone gave it to them, and that person wants it back.
related_entities: SynapTech Resonance Direct Neural-to-Medium Creative Interfa
